abstract: Maintains batch sterility validation logs and analytical contamination assay limits
system_message:
You are Quality Assurance Director (QA). The Quality Assurance Director (QA) oversees quality compliance, maintaining batch sterility validation records and analytical contamination assay thresholds across bioprocessing facilities.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains batch sterility validation logs and analytical contamination assay limits（STERIL）
information_points.content:
QA-STERIL-W2G：For Flanders Microbial Solutions, electronic cycle logging for automated clean-in-place procedures is confirmed in the harvest manifold of the primary fermentation train, and the validated limit of detection for residual cross-contamination between consecutive campaigns is 5 ppm.
QA-STERIL-B57：For Silesian Bioprocess Consortium, electronic cycle logging for automated clean-in-place procedures is confirmed in the harvest manifold of the primary fermentation train, and the validated limit of detection for residual cross-contamination between consecutive campaigns is 5 ppm.
QA-STERIL-OIL：For Rhine Biofermentation Works, electronic cycle logging for automated clean-in-place procedures is confirmed in the harvest manifold of the primary fermentation train, and the validated limit of detection for residual cross-contamination between consecutive campaigns is 8 ppm.

information_points.title: Cleanroom particulate monitoring（AIRMON）
information_points.content:
QA-AIRMON-JEG：For Rhine Biofermentation Works, static qualification logs of the Class A laminar flow hood record a mean cumulative airborne particulate concentration of 30 particles/m3 for particles at least 0.5 micrometers.
QA-AIRMON-KP3：For Flanders Microbial Solutions, static qualification logs of the Class A laminar flow hood record a mean cumulative airborne particulate concentration of 15 particles/m3 for particles at least 0.5 micrometers.
QA-AIRMON-ZYZ：For Silesian Bioprocess Consortium, static qualification logs of the Class A laminar flow hood record a mean cumulative airborne particulate concentration of 55 particles/m3 for particles at least 0.5 micrometers.
